evaluated.name: Intangible Leverage Wedge
evaluated.expression: SUB(RATIO(lt, at), RATIO(lt, ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Book leverage overstates true leverage for firms whose knowledge capital is expensed rather than capitalized; the size of this measurement wedge identifies firms that only look financially fragile.
evaluated.reasoning: The signal is exactly the leverage overstatement caused by omitting a five-year R&D capital stock from the asset base, so it is zero for non-R&D firms and largest for levered intangible-intensive firms. If investors price stated leverage rather than economic leverage, these firms carry an unwarranted distress discount and earn higher subsequent returns. The wedge cannot be produced by either theme alone: it requires both liabilities and an intangible stock adjustment.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: R&D Driven Loss Illusion
evaluated.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(ib), 0), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms reporting accounting losses (a classic distress marker), those whose losses are attributable to discretionary intangible investment are not economically distressed and are mispriced relative to genuine loss-makers.
evaluated.reasoning: The indicator restricts attention to the loss-making distress state, and within it the signal ranks firms by the intensity of expensed R&D and advertising that mechanically depresses reported income. Investors extrapolating negative earnings underreact to the investment nature of these losses, generating positive abnormal returns. Non-loss firms take the value zero, so the effect is purely conditional on the distress state.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Capital Solvency Score
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))
evaluated.hypothesis: A distress score built on intangible-adjusted retained earnings and intangible-adjusted earnings coverage of liabilities separates genuine fragility from accounting fragility better than standard solvency ratios.
evaluated.reasoning: Cumulative R&D expensing permanently depresses retained earnings and current income, mechanically pushing innovative firms into the low-Z-score region of standard distress models. Adding back the R&D stock to retained earnings and R&D flow to earnings before scaling by liabilities restores a solvency measure that reflects real repayment capacity. High values identify firms that are solvent in economic terms but classified as distressed by accounting metrics.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Acquired Intangible Leverage Fragility
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(lt, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Goodwill is purchased rather than internally generated intangible capital; when it is financed with debt it represents genuine fragility, not mismeasured knowledge capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Goodwill-heavy balance sheets provide no cash flow cushion and are prone to impairment exactly when leverage constraints bind, so the joint state of high goodwill and high liabilities marks real default risk rather than accounting distortion. This is the mirror image of the R&D case and should predict low returns, sharpening the distinction between accounting and economic distress within intangible-intensive firms. The product is only large when both conditions hold jointly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: R&D Burn Liquidity Filter
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, oancf), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lct)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among R&D-intensive firms, the binding risk is funding the research program, so internal liquidity net of the annual R&D burn relative to current liabilities separates survivable innovators from fragile ones.
evaluated.reasoning: R&D intensity alone is a weak return predictor because it mixes well-funded innovators with cash-burning firms facing financing risk; scaling cash plus operating cash flow net of the R&D outlay by current liabilities isolates who can self-finance the program. The product is high only for intangible-heavy firms with a genuine liquidity buffer, which should earn the intangible premium without bearing distress losses. Low values flag intangible-heavy firms whose apparent distress is real.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Levered R&D Retrenchment
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt overhang forces genuinely fragile intangible firms to cut research intensity; a multi-year decline in R&D intensity combined with high leverage is a management-revealed signal of true financial distress.
evaluated.reasoning: Managers cut discretionary intangible investment only when funding is genuinely constrained, so the five-year downward trend in R&D-to-sales acts as a revealed-preference distress indicator that accounting ratios miss. Interacted with high liabilities it identifies firms whose knowledge capital is depreciating precisely when they need it most, predicting low future returns. Conversely, low values correspond to levered firms that sustain research intensity, which the market underprices.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Funded Innovation Solvency
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dlc, dltt)), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D intensity is only a benign form of accounting distress when the research program is financed from net cash rather than debt; net-cash-rich innovators are misclassified as fragile by leverage- and earnings-based distress screens.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the additive repair of the multiplicative R&D Burn Liquidity Filter, which delivered the largest alpha (5.4%, t=3.6) but a flat FMB slope because the rank product was degenerate and the oancf term halved coverage. Replacing the product with SUMRANK and operating cash flow with the net-cash position (che minus total debt) preserves the "who can self-fund the research" economics at full coverage and in a form whose cross-sectional slope is interpretable. Expected to keep the portfolio alpha while restoring a strong FMB t-stat.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Adjusted Z Composite
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), RATIO(wcap, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A three-channel distress score in which retained earnings and income are restored for expensed knowledge capital, plus an unadjusted liquidity channel, separates accounting distress from genuine fragility better than a two-channel version.
evaluated.reasoning: The two-channel Knowledge Capital Solvency Score was the archive's best cross-sectional signal (t=4.11) but its alpha was modest, suggesting the score still misranks firms whose adjusted solvency is fine yet whose near-term liquidity is not. Adding working capital to assets — the one Altman channel that is not distorted by intangible expensing — should remove genuinely illiquid firms from the long leg and raise the spread's alpha without diluting the FMB slope.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stable Earnings Innovator
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Genuine financial fragility shows up as volatile profitability, not as a low level of reported profitability; intangible-intensive firms with stable earnings streams carry knowledge capital, whereas intangible-intensive firms with unstable earnings are truly at risk.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive signal measured distress through levels (leverage, coverage, cash), yet default risk is fundamentally about the volatility of the earnings process relative to obligations, which no prior proposal tested. High R&D combined with low five-year ROA volatility identifies firms whose apparent accounting weakness is a stable investment policy rather than an erratic business. This opens a second-moment distress channel that is nearly orthogonal to the level-based composites.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Tangible Collateral Leverage
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt must ultimately be secured by pledgeable assets, so leverage measured against tangible assets only — stripping out capitalized intangibles and goodwill — is the measure of genuine fragility, while book leverage is not.
evaluated.reasoning: The intangible theme enters as a deduction from the collateral base rather than as an addition to profitability, which is the opposite direction of adjustment from all prior proposals and therefore a genuinely distinguishable test. Firms with heavy balance-sheet intangibles and material debt have little liquidation value backing their obligations and should be penalized, whereas the same book leverage backed by hard assets is benign. Winsorizing controls the thin-denominator tail among intangible-dominated balance sheets.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Goodwill Impairment Coverage Risk
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), NEG(RATIO(ib, lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Acquired intangibles are fragile exactly when current earnings do not cover outstanding liabilities, because weak earnings trigger impairment tests that crystallize the loss and tighten covenants.
evaluated.reasoning: The multiplicative goodwill-leverage signal produced a reliable negative alpha (t=-2.96) but no cross-sectional slope, so this version keeps the acquired-intangible fragility channel while switching the distress leg from static leverage to earnings coverage of liabilities and the combination form to SUMRANK. This changes the economic trigger from balance-sheet stock to flow-based impairment risk, and should convert the existing portfolio evidence into cross-sectional evidence as well.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Funded Deleveraging
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(GROWTH(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that simultaneously expand research intensity and reduce their liability ratio are revealing internally generated funding capacity, the cleanest observable separation of accounting distress from genuine fragility.
evaluated.reasoning: The prior dynamic signal (Levered R&D Retrenchment) had real portfolio content (alpha t=-2.69) but no FMB slope because it multiplied a rank by a noisy five-year trend; this version uses contemporaneous one-year changes in both legs combined additively, so the state is a revealed-preference joint action rather than a skewed product. Managers only raise research spending while paying down liabilities when internal cash generation is genuinely strong, which distress screens based on levels cannot observe. It tests the change dimension rather than the level dimension of the same economic story.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Capital Solvency With Intensity
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The mispricing is largest for firms that are simultaneously intangible-intensive and economically solvent once knowledge capital is restored; intensity identifies who is misclassified, adjusted solvency identifies who is genuinely safe.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive shows the R&D-intensity leg drives FF5 alpha (4.7–4.9%) while the adjusted retained-earnings and coverage legs drive the cross-sectional slope (t>4), and no signal has yet carried all three. Combining them additively should retain the FMB slope of the Z-composite while lifting alpha toward the intensity-based signals. This is the direct consolidation test of the two evidence channels the archive has separated.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Industry Neutral Intangible Solvency
evaluated.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible intensity and leverage norms are largely industry attributes, so the accounting-versus-genuine distress distinction is meaningful only relative to industry peers; neutralizing industry should sharpen the signal and stabilize the spread portfolio.
evaluated.reasoning: The best signals so far have low Sharpe relative to their alpha, which is the signature of a spread that is long software/biotech and short capital-intensive industries and therefore carries large uncompensated sector risk. Demeaning each leg within industry isolates the firm-specific component of intangible-adjusted solvency and tests whether the existing FMB evidence survives without the industry tilt. It isolates one specific design choice — industry neutralization — on the archive's best-performing formula family.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Pre Innovation Profit Coverage
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)
evaluated.hypothesis: The correct measure of debt-servicing capacity for an intangible-intensive firm is profit measured before discretionary knowledge investment, since R&D can be cut in a crisis; scaled by total liabilities this ranks true fragility rather than accounting fragility.
evaluated.reasoning: No prior proposal has used gross profitability, the profitability measure least contaminated by intangible expensing, and adding R&D back makes explicit that research spending is discretionary cash rather than a fixed obligation. As a single clean ratio with full coverage it avoids the degenerate distributions that killed the indicator and product-form signals, and it should produce an interpretable, monotone cross-sectional slope. It tests whether the coverage channel works better with a pre-intangible-investment numerator than with net income.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Tax Revealed Solvency Of Innovators
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(txt, lt))
evaluated.hypothesis: Tax expense is a hard, cash-verified signal of economic profit that accounting distress metrics miss; an intangible-heavy firm that still books meaningful taxes against its liabilities owns productive knowledge capital rather than being fragile.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive signal has measured profitability with reported income, which is precisely the number distorted by intangible expensing and loss carryforwards; the tax line is a different, less manipulable observation of the same underlying profitability. Pairing a five-year knowledge-capital stock with tax-to-liabilities creates a separation between innovators generating taxable income and innovators generating only accounting losses. This opens a data channel (txt) untouched by the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt Financed Intangible Expansion
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible investment scaled up at the same time liabilities are expanding is overextension rather than resilience, because knowledge capital provides no collateral and the cash outflow is immediate while payoffs are distant.
evaluated.reasoning: The prior dynamic signal used GROWTH on a COALESCE-zero base, which was undefined for zero-R&D firms and cut coverage to 0.051, and its realized sign was the opposite of the hypothesis; DELTA is well defined at zero and restores full coverage. Reorienting the hypothesis to match the evidence — rising intangible outlays financed by rising liabilities predicts low returns — turns the earlier failure into a testable overextension mechanism. This is the repair plus sign-reversal experiment the archive calls for.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Solvency Position In Own History
evaluated.expression: TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), 5)
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters for genuine fragility is where a firm's intangible-adjusted debt coverage sits relative to its own recent history, since a permanently low but stable ratio is a business model while a deteriorating one is real distress.
evaluated.reasoning: All archive signals rank firms against each other on levels, which mechanically penalizes intangible-intensive business models that have always looked weak; the within-firm historical position removes that permanent component and isolates deterioration. If this delivers independent predictive power, it identifies a time-series conditioning dimension that can later be combined with the cross-sectional level composites. It is a deliberately clean single-mechanism test rather than a blended score.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovator Solvency Triple Score
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The cleanest separation of accounting from genuine distress combines who is misclassified (R&D intensity), whether accumulated knowledge capital restores the balance sheet (adjusted retained earnings), and whether pre-innovation profit actually covers obligations.
evaluated.reasoning: The current leader pairs intensity with net-income coverage (alpha 4.4%), while the standalone gross-profit-plus-R&D coverage ratio produced a larger alpha (4.7%) with better Sharpe, so substituting the stronger coverage channel into the leading three-leg structure should dominate both. Gross profit is measured before the intangible expensing that creates the distress illusion, making it the economically correct debt-service numerator for this theme. This is the head-to-head consolidation of the archive's two best mechanisms.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Adjusted Balance Sheet Plus Gross Coverage
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))
evaluated.hypothesis: Stock-based (knowledge-capital-restored retained earnings) and flow-based (pre-innovation profit coverage) solvency are the two economically necessary legs; R&D intensity may add only a factor tilt rather than incremental information.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates one design choice against Signal 1 — the presence of the raw intensity leg — so the pair jointly identifies whether the intensity channel contributes genuine mispricing information or merely levers the sector exposure that raises alpha while depressing Sharpe. It is otherwise the direct numerator upgrade of the gen-0 Knowledge Capital Solvency Score, replacing net income with pre-innovation gross profit. Full coverage and a linear rank form keep the cross-sectional slope interpretable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Post Innovation Profit Coverage
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)
evaluated.hypothesis: If the theme's core claim is right, deducting rather than adding back research spending should weaken predictive power, because the deduction re-imposes exactly the accounting distortion that makes innovators look distressed.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the deliberate mirror of Pre-Innovation Profit Coverage and is the sharpest available test of whether the intangible add-back — not gross profitability per se — is the source of the abnormal return. A materially weaker result confirms the add-back is the active ingredient and justifies pushing the add-back into other channels; a similar result would tell us the coverage effect is generic profitability and would redirect the search. Cheap, full coverage, and highly diagnostic for the remaining generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stability Weighted Knowledge Solvency
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)), SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Genuine fragility is the volatility of the earnings process relative to a fixed obligation, so an intangible-intensive firm with restored book equity and a stable earnings stream is safe even with weak reported profitability.
evaluated.reasoning: The earnings-volatility leg produced the archive's single best alpha t-stat (4.09) but a poor Sharpe when paired only with intensity, suggesting it needs a solvency-level anchor to stabilize portfolio composition. Combining the second-moment distress channel with the first-moment adjusted balance sheet tests whether the two are complementary rather than substitutes. This keeps the highest-alpha ingredient in play while addressing its diagnosed weakness.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Unpledgeable Assets Debt Burden
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt secured by a balance sheet dominated by purchased intangibles carries high deadweight distress costs because those assets lose most of their value outside the firm; this is genuine fragility, distinct from the benign accounting distress of R&D expensers.
evaluated.reasoning: Both prior versions of this short-side mechanism produced reliable negative alphas (t=−3.08 and −2.96) but essentially zero FMB slope, which the goodwill experiment showed is a symptom of multiplicative or thin-denominator construction rather than a bad economic story. Recasting it as a rank-sum of intangible asset share and debt over tangible collateral should preserve the alpha while producing a usable cross-sectional slope. It is the complementary short leg to the R&D-based long side.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Weakest Link Innovator Solvency
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Default is triggered by the binding constraint, so a firm is genuinely safe only if intangible-adjusted earnings coverage and near-term working-capital liquidity are both adequate; the minimum of the two is the economically correct aggregator.
evaluated.reasoning: Every composite so far averages ranks, which lets a strong solvency leg mask a fatal liquidity shortfall — precisely the error that would put genuinely fragile intangible firms in the long leg. The MIN aggregator implements a conjunction without the degenerate zero mass and skewness that ruined the earlier multiplicative signals, and it should improve the long leg's composition and therefore the Sharpe ratio. It tests aggregator structure, a lever the archive has not yet varied.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Weakest Link Gross Coverage
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely safe only if pre-innovation profit covers its obligations and its working capital is adequate; gross profit plus R&D is the debt-service numerator least contaminated by intangible expensing.
evaluated.reasoning: This substitutes the archive's strongest coverage numerator (pre-innovation profit, 4.7% standalone alpha) into the archive's strongest aggregator (MIN, 5.8% alpha), holding the liquidity leg fixed so the comparison isolates exactly one design choice. Net income is transitory and negative for many healthy innovators, so replacing it with gross profit before research spending should sharpen the conjunction and reduce misclassification in the long leg. Expected to improve both alpha and the FMB slope relative to the gen-3 leader.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Triple Constraint Solvency Minimum
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Genuine safety requires a restored balance sheet, adequate earnings coverage, and adequate liquidity simultaneously; failing any one constraint is sufficient for real fragility regardless of the other two.
evaluated.reasoning: The two-leg MIN beat every averaged composite, so the open question is whether conjunction depth continues to help or whether a third binding constraint makes the long leg too restrictive and unstable. Adding the knowledge-capital-restored retained earnings leg — the ingredient behind the archive's best FMB slopes — is the economically motivated third constraint. The result tells us whether to keep deepening conjunctions or stop at two legs in the consolidation phase.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Conjunction Safety With Intensity Tilt
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Conjunction identifies which firms are genuinely safe, while R&D intensity identifies which safe firms are most likely to be misclassified as distressed by conventional accounting; the mispricing is concentrated where both hold.
evaluated.reasoning: Across the archive the intensity leg has consistently added roughly one percentage point of alpha (3.3%→4.4%, 3.4%→4.7%) whenever appended to a solvency score, and it has never yet been paired with the MIN aggregator. Averaging the conjunction score with intensity preserves the safety screen while tilting the long leg toward firms whose accounting distress is illusory. This is the highest-expected-value consolidation available given the evidence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Collateral And Coverage Minimum
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Genuine fragility is the joint failure of pledgeable-asset backing and profit coverage of liabilities; firms weak on either dimension are truly distressed, whereas intangible-heavy firms strong on both are only accounting-distressed.
evaluated.reasoning: The collateral channel has twice generated reliable negative alpha but no cross-sectional slope, consistent with a relationship that only bites in the joint tail rather than monotonically — exactly the situation the MIN aggregator is designed for. Recasting tangible-asset coverage as one leg of a conjunction with pre-innovation profit coverage should finally deliver a slope alongside the alpha. It also converts the short-side mechanism into a long-side-tradable, full-sample variable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Total Brand And Research Capital Solvency
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), COALESCE(xad, 0)), lt))
evaluated.hypothesis: Advertising builds brand capital that is expensed exactly like research, so the accounting-distress illusion extends to advertising-intensive firms and the add-back should include both intangible outlays.
evaluated.reasoning: Every successful signal in the archive has adjusted only for R&D, leaving consumer-facing brand builders — a large group of apparently low-profitability, high-liability firms — unadjusted and therefore misranked. Including advertising in both the intensity leg and the earnings add-back tests whether the mechanism is about research specifically or about expensed intangible investment generally. The answer determines whether the remaining generations should broaden or narrow the intangible definition.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Capital Versus Rollover Risk
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), lt), NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms fail when short-term debt must be refinanced against assets lenders cannot seize; large knowledge capital relative to total liabilities combined with low reliance on maturing debt marks accounting rather than genuine distress.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has treated liabilities as a single stock and never distinguished maturing obligations, yet rollover risk is the specific channel through which intangible firms are forced into distress, since knowledge capital cannot be pledged to refinance. Pairing a shadow-collateral ratio (five-year R&D stock over liabilities) with the share of current assets pre-committed to short-term debt opens the maturity dimension. It is economically distinct from every coverage- and liquidity-based signal already tested.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Maturity Constrained Knowledge Solvency
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: For an intangible-intensive firm the binding constraint is refinancing maturing debt against unpledgeable assets, so rollover exposure belongs inside the conjunction alongside restored book equity and adjusted earnings coverage.
evaluated.reasoning: The rollover leg delivered the archive's highest alpha t-stat (4.31) but no slope when averaged, which is the signature of a variable that matters only when it binds — precisely what the MIN aggregator captures. This substitutes maturity risk for the working-capital leg in the winning triple, so the comparison against Triple Constraint Solvency Minimum cleanly identifies which liquidity concept is the true binding constraint. If the slope holds near 4.5 with alpha rising toward 5.7%, this dominates the current leader.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Buffered Knowledge Solvency
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash, not accrual working capital, is the survival buffer for research-intensive firms whose current assets are thin and whose spending is a continuous cash outflow.
evaluated.reasoning: The working-capital leg (act−lct) costs roughly two percentage points of coverage and is dominated by receivables and inventory — items that barely exist for the intangible-intensive firms this theme targets — whereas cash-to-liabilities is available for essentially every firm and is the buffer that actually funds R&D through a downturn. This isolates the liquidity-leg definition while restoring coverage from 0.122 toward 0.145. A stable or improved slope with fuller coverage would make the conjunction family more robust rather than merely better fitted.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Conjunction Plus Restored Book Equity
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Solvency constraints (coverage, liquidity) are binding conditions best combined by conjunction, while the knowledge-capital-restored balance sheet is a graded valuation input best combined additively.
evaluated.reasoning: Triple Constraint put restored retained earnings *inside* the MIN, which raised the slope but trimmed alpha relative to the two-leg version; this variant places the same leg additively outside the conjunction so the pair identifies whether the balance-sheet channel acts as a hard constraint or as a graded signal. Aggregator placement is the one structural lever the archive has not yet resolved, and it plausibly recovers the 5.8% alpha while retaining a slope above 4. It is a targeted structural test, not a cosmetic variant.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Distress Misclassification Gap
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(ib, lt))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), RANK(RATIO(re, at))))

considered.hypothesis: Goodwill is purchased rather than internally generated intangible capital; when it is financed with debt it represents genuine fragility, not mismeasured knowledge capital.
considered.reasoning: Goodwill-heavy balance sheets provide no cash flow cushion and are prone to impairment exactly when leverage constraints bind, so the joint state of high goodwill and high liabilities marks real default risk rather than accounting distortion. This is the mirror image of the R&D case and should predict low returns, sharpening the distinction between accounting and economic distress within intangible-intensive firms. The product is only large when both conditions hold jointly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: R&D Burn Liquidity Filter
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, oancf), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lct)))
considered.hypothesis: Among R&D-intensive firms, the binding risk is funding the research program, so internal liquidity net of the annual R&D burn relative to current liabilities separates survivable innovators from fragile ones.
considered.reasoning: R&D intensity alone is a weak return predictor because it mixes well-funded innovators with cash-burning firms facing financing risk; scaling cash plus operating cash flow net of the R&D outlay by current liabilities isolates who can self-finance the program. The product is high only for intangible-heavy firms with a genuine liquidity buffer, which should earn the intangible premium without bearing distress losses. Low values flag intangible-heavy firms whose apparent distress is real.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Levered R&D Retrenchment
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt overhang forces genuinely fragile intangible firms to cut research intensity; a multi-year decline in R&D intensity combined with high leverage is a management-revealed signal of true financial distress.
considered.reasoning: Managers cut discretionary intangible investment only when funding is genuinely constrained, so the five-year downward trend in R&D-to-sales acts as a revealed-preference distress indicator that accounting ratios miss. Interacted with high liabilities it identifies firms whose knowledge capital is depreciating precisely when they need it most, predicting low future returns. Conversely, low values correspond to levered firms that sustain research intensity, which the market underprices.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Funded Innovation Solvency
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dlc, dltt)), at))
considered.hypothesis: R&D intensity is only a benign form of accounting distress when the research program is financed from net cash rather than debt; net-cash-rich innovators are misclassified as fragile by leverage- and earnings-based distress screens.
considered.reasoning: This is the additive repair of the multiplicative R&D Burn Liquidity Filter, which delivered the largest alpha (5.4%, t=3.6) but a flat FMB slope because the rank product was degenerate and the oancf term halved coverage. Replacing the product with SUMRANK and operating cash flow with the net-cash position (che minus total debt) preserves the "who can self-fund the research" economics at full coverage and in a form whose cross-sectional slope is interpretable. Expected to keep the portfolio alpha while restoring a strong FMB t-stat.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Adjusted Z Composite
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), RATIO(wcap, at)))
considered.hypothesis: A three-channel distress score in which retained earnings and income are restored for expensed knowledge capital, plus an unadjusted liquidity channel, separates accounting distress from genuine fragility better than a two-channel version.
considered.reasoning: The two-channel Knowledge Capital Solvency Score was the archive's best cross-sectional signal (t=4.11) but its alpha was modest, suggesting the score still misranks firms whose adjusted solvency is fine yet whose near-term liquidity is not. Adding working capital to assets — the one Altman channel that is not distorted by intangible expensing — should remove genuinely illiquid firms from the long leg and raise the spread's alpha without diluting the FMB slope.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stable Earnings Innovator
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine financial fragility shows up as volatile profitability, not as a low level of reported profitability; intangible-intensive firms with stable earnings streams carry knowledge capital, whereas intangible-intensive firms with unstable earnings are truly at risk.
considered.reasoning: Every archive signal measured distress through levels (leverage, coverage, cash), yet default risk is fundamentally about the volatility of the earnings process relative to obligations, which no prior proposal tested. High R&D combined with low five-year ROA volatility identifies firms whose apparent accounting weakness is a stable investment policy rather than an erratic business. This opens a second-moment distress channel that is nearly orthogonal to the level-based composites.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Tangible Collateral Leverage
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Debt must ultimately be secured by pledgeable assets, so leverage measured against tangible assets only — stripping out capitalized intangibles and goodwill — is the measure of genuine fragility, while book leverage is not.
considered.reasoning: The intangible theme enters as a deduction from the collateral base rather than as an addition to profitability, which is the opposite direction of adjustment from all prior proposals and therefore a genuinely distinguishable test. Firms with heavy balance-sheet intangibles and material debt have little liquidation value backing their obligations and should be penalized, whereas the same book leverage backed by hard assets is benign. Winsorizing controls the thin-denominator tail among intangible-dominated balance sheets.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Impairment Coverage Risk
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), NEG(RATIO(ib, lt)))
considered.hypothesis: Acquired intangibles are fragile exactly when current earnings do not cover outstanding liabilities, because weak earnings trigger impairment tests that crystallize the loss and tighten covenants.
considered.reasoning: The multiplicative goodwill-leverage signal produced a reliable negative alpha (t=-2.96) but no cross-sectional slope, so this version keeps the acquired-intangible fragility channel while switching the distress leg from static leverage to earnings coverage of liabilities and the combination form to SUMRANK. This changes the economic trigger from balance-sheet stock to flow-based impairment risk, and should convert the existing portfolio evidence into cross-sectional evidence as well.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation Funded Deleveraging
considered.expression: SUMRANK(GROWTH(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that simultaneously expand research intensity and reduce their liability ratio are revealing internally generated funding capacity, the cleanest observable separation of accounting distress from genuine fragility.
considered.reasoning: The prior dynamic signal (Levered R&D Retrenchment) had real portfolio content (alpha t=-2.69) but no FMB slope because it multiplied a rank by a noisy five-year trend; this version uses contemporaneous one-year changes in both legs combined additively, so the state is a revealed-preference joint action rather than a skewed product. Managers only raise research spending while paying down liabilities when internal cash generation is genuinely strong, which distress screens based on levels cannot observe. It tests the change dimension rather than the level dimension of the same economic story.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Capital Solvency With Intensity
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: The mispricing is largest for firms that are simultaneously intangible-intensive and economically solvent once knowledge capital is restored; intensity identifies who is misclassified, adjusted solvency identifies who is genuinely safe.
considered.reasoning: The archive shows the R&D-intensity leg drives FF5 alpha (4.7–4.9%) while the adjusted retained-earnings and coverage legs drive the cross-sectional slope (t>4), and no signal has yet carried all three. Combining them additively should retain the FMB slope of the Z-composite while lifting alpha toward the intensity-based signals. This is the direct consolidation test of the two evidence channels the archive has separated.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Industry Neutral Intangible Solvency
considered.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: Intangible intensity and leverage norms are largely industry attributes, so the accounting-versus-genuine distress distinction is meaningful only relative to industry peers; neutralizing industry should sharpen the signal and stabilize the spread portfolio.
considered.reasoning: The best signals so far have low Sharpe relative to their alpha, which is the signature of a spread that is long software/biotech and short capital-intensive industries and therefore carries large uncompensated sector risk. Demeaning each leg within industry isolates the firm-specific component of intangible-adjusted solvency and tests whether the existing FMB evidence survives without the industry tilt. It isolates one specific design choice — industry neutralization — on the archive's best-performing formula family.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Pre Innovation Profit Coverage
considered.expression: RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)
considered.hypothesis: The correct measure of debt-servicing capacity for an intangible-intensive firm is profit measured before discretionary knowledge investment, since R&D can be cut in a crisis; scaled by total liabilities this ranks true fragility rather than accounting fragility.
considered.reasoning: No prior proposal has used gross profitability, the profitability measure least contaminated by intangible expensing, and adding R&D back makes explicit that research spending is discretionary cash rather than a fixed obligation. As a single clean ratio with full coverage it avoids the degenerate distributions that killed the indicator and product-form signals, and it should produce an interpretable, monotone cross-sectional slope. It tests whether the coverage channel works better with a pre-intangible-investment numerator than with net income.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Tax Revealed Solvency Of Innovators
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(txt, lt))
considered.hypothesis: Tax expense is a hard, cash-verified signal of economic profit that accounting distress metrics miss; an intangible-heavy firm that still books meaningful taxes against its liabilities owns productive knowledge capital rather than being fragile.
considered.reasoning: Every archive signal has measured profitability with reported income, which is precisely the number distorted by intangible expensing and loss carryforwards; the tax line is a different, less manipulable observation of the same underlying profitability. Pairing a five-year knowledge-capital stock with tax-to-liabilities creates a separation between innovators generating taxable income and innovators generating only accounting losses. This opens a data channel (txt) untouched by the archive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Financed Intangible Expansion
considered.expression: SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Intangible investment scaled up at the same time liabilities are expanding is overextension rather than resilience, because knowledge capital provides no collateral and the cash outflow is immediate while payoffs are distant.
considered.reasoning: The prior dynamic signal used GROWTH on a COALESCE-zero base, which was undefined for zero-R&D firms and cut coverage to 0.051, and its realized sign was the opposite of the hypothesis; DELTA is well defined at zero and restores full coverage. Reorienting the hypothesis to match the evidence — rising intangible outlays financed by rising liabilities predicts low returns — turns the earlier failure into a testable overextension mechanism. This is the repair plus sign-reversal experiment the archive calls for.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Solvency Position In Own History
considered.expression: TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), 5)
considered.hypothesis: What matters for genuine fragility is where a firm's intangible-adjusted debt coverage sits relative to its own recent history, since a permanently low but stable ratio is a business model while a deteriorating one is real distress.
considered.reasoning: All archive signals rank firms against each other on levels, which mechanically penalizes intangible-intensive business models that have always looked weak; the within-firm historical position removes that permanent component and isolates deterioration. If this delivers independent predictive power, it identifies a time-series conditioning dimension that can later be combined with the cross-sectional level composites. It is a deliberately clean single-mechanism test rather than a blended score.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovator Solvency Triple Score
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: The cleanest separation of accounting from genuine distress combines who is misclassified (R&D intensity), whether accumulated knowledge capital restores the balance sheet (adjusted retained earnings), and whether pre-innovation profit actually covers obligations.
considered.reasoning: The current leader pairs intensity with net-income coverage (alpha 4.4%), while the standalone gross-profit-plus-R&D coverage ratio produced a larger alpha (4.7%) with better Sharpe, so substituting the stronger coverage channel into the leading three-leg structure should dominate both. Gross profit is measured before the intangible expensing that creates the distress illusion, making it the economically correct debt-service numerator for this theme. This is the head-to-head consolidation of the archive's two best mechanisms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Adjusted Balance Sheet Plus Gross Coverage
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))
considered.hypothesis: Stock-based (knowledge-capital-restored retained earnings) and flow-based (pre-innovation profit coverage) solvency are the two economically necessary legs; R&D intensity may add only a factor tilt rather than incremental information.
considered.reasoning: This isolates one design choice against Signal 1 — the presence of the raw intensity leg — so the pair jointly identifies whether the intensity channel contributes genuine mispricing information or merely levers the sector exposure that raises alpha while depressing Sharpe. It is otherwise the direct numerator upgrade of the gen-0 Knowledge Capital Solvency Score, replacing net income with pre-innovation gross profit. Full coverage and a linear rank form keep the cross-sectional slope interpretable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Post Innovation Profit Coverage
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)
considered.hypothesis: If the theme's core claim is right, deducting rather than adding back research spending should weaken predictive power, because the deduction re-imposes exactly the accounting distortion that makes innovators look distressed.
considered.reasoning: This is the deliberate mirror of Pre-Innovation Profit Coverage and is the sharpest available test of whether the intangible add-back — not gross profitability per se — is the source of the abnormal return. A materially weaker result confirms the add-back is the active ingredient and justifies pushing the add-back into other channels; a similar result would tell us the coverage effect is generic profitability and would redirect the search. Cheap, full coverage, and highly diagnostic for the remaining generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stability Weighted Knowledge Solvency
considered.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)), SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine fragility is the volatility of the earnings process relative to a fixed obligation, so an intangible-intensive firm with restored book equity and a stable earnings stream is safe even with weak reported profitability.
considered.reasoning: The earnings-volatility leg produced the archive's single best alpha t-stat (4.09) but a poor Sharpe when paired only with intensity, suggesting it needs a solvency-level anchor to stabilize portfolio composition. Combining the second-moment distress channel with the first-moment adjusted balance sheet tests whether the two are complementary rather than substitutes. This keeps the highest-alpha ingredient in play while addressing its diagnosed weakness.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Unpledgeable Assets Debt Burden
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt secured by a balance sheet dominated by purchased intangibles carries high deadweight distress costs because those assets lose most of their value outside the firm; this is genuine fragility, distinct from the benign accounting distress of R&D expensers.
considered.reasoning: Both prior versions of this short-side mechanism produced reliable negative alphas (t=−3.08 and −2.96) but essentially zero FMB slope, which the goodwill experiment showed is a symptom of multiplicative or thin-denominator construction rather than a bad economic story. Recasting it as a rank-sum of intangible asset share and debt over tangible collateral should preserve the alpha while producing a usable cross-sectional slope. It is the complementary short leg to the R&D-based long side.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Weakest Link Innovator Solvency
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: Default is triggered by the binding constraint, so a firm is genuinely safe only if intangible-adjusted earnings coverage and near-term working-capital liquidity are both adequate; the minimum of the two is the economically correct aggregator.
considered.reasoning: Every composite so far averages ranks, which lets a strong solvency leg mask a fatal liquidity shortfall — precisely the error that would put genuinely fragile intangible firms in the long leg. The MIN aggregator implements a conjunction without the degenerate zero mass and skewness that ruined the earlier multiplicative signals, and it should improve the long leg's composition and therefore the Sharpe ratio. It tests aggregator structure, a lever the archive has not yet varied.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Weakest Link Gross Coverage
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely safe only if pre-innovation profit covers its obligations and its working capital is adequate; gross profit plus R&D is the debt-service numerator least contaminated by intangible expensing.
considered.reasoning: This substitutes the archive's strongest coverage numerator (pre-innovation profit, 4.7% standalone alpha) into the archive's strongest aggregator (MIN, 5.8% alpha), holding the liquidity leg fixed so the comparison isolates exactly one design choice. Net income is transitory and negative for many healthy innovators, so replacing it with gross profit before research spending should sharpen the conjunction and reduce misclassification in the long leg. Expected to improve both alpha and the FMB slope relative to the gen-3 leader.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Triple Constraint Solvency Minimum
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine safety requires a restored balance sheet, adequate earnings coverage, and adequate liquidity simultaneously; failing any one constraint is sufficient for real fragility regardless of the other two.
considered.reasoning: The two-leg MIN beat every averaged composite, so the open question is whether conjunction depth continues to help or whether a third binding constraint makes the long leg too restrictive and unstable. Adding the knowledge-capital-restored retained earnings leg — the ingredient behind the archive's best FMB slopes — is the economically motivated third constraint. The result tells us whether to keep deepening conjunctions or stop at two legs in the consolidation phase.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Conjunction Safety With Intensity Tilt
considered.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))
considered.hypothesis: Conjunction identifies which firms are genuinely safe, while R&D intensity identifies which safe firms are most likely to be misclassified as distressed by conventional accounting; the mispricing is concentrated where both hold.
considered.reasoning: Across the archive the intensity leg has consistently added roughly one percentage point of alpha (3.3%→4.4%, 3.4%→4.7%) whenever appended to a solvency score, and it has never yet been paired with the MIN aggregator. Averaging the conjunction score with intensity preserves the safety screen while tilting the long leg toward firms whose accounting distress is illusory. This is the highest-expected-value consolidation available given the evidence.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Collateral And Coverage Minimum
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine fragility is the joint failure of pledgeable-asset backing and profit coverage of liabilities; firms weak on either dimension are truly distressed, whereas intangible-heavy firms strong on both are only accounting-distressed.
considered.reasoning: The collateral channel has twice generated reliable negative alpha but no cross-sectional slope, consistent with a relationship that only bites in the joint tail rather than monotonically — exactly the situation the MIN aggregator is designed for. Recasting tangible-asset coverage as one leg of a conjunction with pre-innovation profit coverage should finally deliver a slope alongside the alpha. It also converts the short-side mechanism into a long-side-tradable, full-sample variable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Total Brand And Research Capital Solvency
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), COALESCE(xad, 0)), lt))
considered.hypothesis: Advertising builds brand capital that is expensed exactly like research, so the accounting-distress illusion extends to advertising-intensive firms and the add-back should include both intangible outlays.
considered.reasoning: Every successful signal in the archive has adjusted only for R&D, leaving consumer-facing brand builders — a large group of apparently low-profitability, high-liability firms — unadjusted and therefore misranked. Including advertising in both the intensity leg and the earnings add-back tests whether the mechanism is about research specifically or about expensed intangible investment generally. The answer determines whether the remaining generations should broaden or narrow the intangible definition.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Capital Versus Rollover Risk
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), lt), NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))
considered.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms fail when short-term debt must be refinanced against assets lenders cannot seize; large knowledge capital relative to total liabilities combined with low reliance on maturing debt marks accounting rather than genuine distress.
considered.reasoning: The archive has treated liabilities as a single stock and never distinguished maturing obligations, yet rollover risk is the specific channel through which intangible firms are forced into distress, since knowledge capital cannot be pledged to refinance. Pairing a shadow-collateral ratio (five-year R&D stock over liabilities) with the share of current assets pre-committed to short-term debt opens the maturity dimension. It is economically distinct from every coverage- and liquidity-based signal already tested.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Maturity Constrained Knowledge Solvency
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))))
considered.hypothesis: For an intangible-intensive firm the binding constraint is refinancing maturing debt against unpledgeable assets, so rollover exposure belongs inside the conjunction alongside restored book equity and adjusted earnings coverage.
considered.reasoning: The rollover leg delivered the archive's highest alpha t-stat (4.31) but no slope when averaged, which is the signature of a variable that matters only when it binds — precisely what the MIN aggregator captures. This substitutes maturity risk for the working-capital leg in the winning triple, so the comparison against Triple Constraint Solvency Minimum cleanly identifies which liquidity concept is the true binding constraint. If the slope holds near 4.5 with alpha rising toward 5.7%, this dominates the current leader.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Buffered Knowledge Solvency
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Cash, not accrual working capital, is the survival buffer for research-intensive firms whose current assets are thin and whose spending is a continuous cash outflow.
considered.reasoning: The working-capital leg (act−lct) costs roughly two percentage points of coverage and is dominated by receivables and inventory — items that barely exist for the intangible-intensive firms this theme targets — whereas cash-to-liabilities is available for essentially every firm and is the buffer that actually funds R&D through a downturn. This isolates the liquidity-leg definition while restoring coverage from 0.122 toward 0.145. A stable or improved slope with fuller coverage would make the conjunction family more robust rather than merely better fitted.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Conjunction Plus Restored Book Equity
considered.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at))
considered.hypothesis: Solvency constraints (coverage, liquidity) are binding conditions best combined by conjunction, while the knowledge-capital-restored balance sheet is a graded valuation input best combined additively.
considered.reasoning: Triple Constraint put restored retained earnings *inside* the MIN, which raised the slope but trimmed alpha relative to the two-leg version; this variant places the same leg additively outside the conjunction so the pair identifies whether the balance-sheet channel acts as a hard constraint or as a graded signal. Aggregator placement is the one structural lever the archive has not yet resolved, and it plausibly recovers the 5.8% alpha while retaining a slope above 4. It is a targeted structural test, not a cosmetic variant.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Distress Misclassification Gap
considered.expression: SUMRANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(ib, lt))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), RANK(RATIO(re, at))))
considered.hypothesis: The mispricing is proportional to how far a firm's distress ranking improves once expensed knowledge capital is restored to earnings and book equity; that rank improvement is a direct measure of being misclassified by conventional accounting.
considered.reasoning: Every archive signal measures the *level* of adjusted solvency, which conflates being safe with being intangible-intensive, whereas the difference between adjusted and unadjusted ranks isolates the accounting distortion itself — the exact object the theme names. The gen-0 level-based wedge failed only because unscaled differences produced a degenerate distribution; rank differences are bounded, well spread, and available at full coverage. If this carries independent power it becomes the cleanest statement of the mechanism.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Misclassified But Genuinely Solvent
considered.expression: SUMRANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(ib, lt))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Abnormal returns accrue to firms that are simultaneously misclassified by conventional distress accounting and genuinely solvent once every binding constraint is checked; either condition alone is insufficient.
considered.reasoning: This is the literal formulation of the research question — the misclassification gap identifies who looks wrongly distressed, and the conjunction score verifies that the apparent safety is real rather than another accounting artifact. It pairs the archive's best aggregator with the one economic quantity the archive has never measured, so a strong result would be attributable to the interaction rather than to either level effect. Together with Signal 4 it also attributes performance between the gap's standalone power and its complementarity with the safety screen.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Binding Fragility Maximum
considered.expression: MAX(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely fragile if its worst dimension is bad — either debt vastly exceeds pledgeable assets or profit before knowledge investment fails to cover liabilities — so the maximum of fragility ranks is the correct short-side aggregator.
considered.reasoning: Three separate collateral- and goodwill-based short signals produced reliable negative alphas (t between −2.96 and −3.73) but essentially zero FMB slopes, indicating a relationship concentrated in the joint tail rather than monotone in either variable — the exact structure MAX encodes, mirroring the MIN success on the long side. Using tangible-asset-backed leverage and pre-innovation profit coverage keeps the two themes explicitly interacted. If MAX delivers a slope, the framework becomes symmetric and the long-short spread can be built from both ends.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Four Constraint Innovator Safety
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(che, lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))))
considered.hypothesis: An intangible-intensive firm is genuinely safe only if restored book equity, adjusted earnings coverage, cash buffer, and refinancing exposure are all adequate; the two liquidity constraints are complements, not substitutes, because cash protects against burn while low maturing debt protects against rollover.
considered.reasoning: The cash leg and the maturity leg each independently lifted the FMB slope above 4.5 with alphas near 4.7%, so the untested question is whether they capture different failure modes and therefore stack. Conjunction is the only aggregator that has preserved slopes while adding legs, and each additional constraint has so far removed genuinely fragile firms from the long leg rather than merely shrinking it. This is the natural terminal depth test for the winning family.

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), lct)))))
considered.hypothesis: For an intangible-intensive firm, next year's research budget is a de facto obligation alongside current liabilities, so the correct liquidity constraint is cash relative to current liabilities plus the R&D commitment.
considered.reasoning: Every liquidity leg tested so far treats research spending as free, yet cutting R&D is exactly what destroys the knowledge capital the long leg is supposed to own — so the denominator should include it. This makes the liquidity constraint theme-specific rather than generic, sharpening the separation between innovators who can sustain their programs and those who will be forced to retrench. It isolates the liquidity denominator while holding the rest of the winning triple fixed.

considered.name: Safety Minus Fragility Spread
considered.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))), NEG(MAX(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))))))

Netting the fragility score against the safety score should produce a spread whose short leg is populated by genuinely fragile intangible-heavy borrowers rather than merely low-coverage firms. This is a structural composition test rather than a new variable.

considered.name: Stability Constrained Innovator Safety
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine fragility is the volatility of the earnings process relative to fixed obligations, so earnings instability should act as a disqualifying constraint rather than as an averaged score component.

It is the last unexploited high-alpha ingredient in the archive.

considered.expression: MAX(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), MAX(RANK(RATIO(dlc, act)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))))

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(txt, lt))))

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(dlc, lct)))))

considered.expression: MAX(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)))), MAX(RANK(RATIO(dlc, act)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))))

considered.name: Smoothed Earnings Coverage Constraint
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))))

considered.reasoning: The coverage leg is the one component of the winning triple whose input is transitory, and misclassifying a temporarily loss-making innovator as constrained is exactly the error this theme is designed to avoid. Smoothing should reduce turnover in the long leg and raise both the slope and the Sharpe ratio relative to Maturity-Constrained Knowledge Solvency, while changing nothing else. It is a timing test on the archive's leading signal.

considered.expression: SUMRANK(MAX(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), MAX(RANK(RATIO(dlc, act)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))))), RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at))

considered.name: Smoothed Coverage Near Term Cash
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(dlc, lct)))))

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))

Pairing it with the smoothing improvement isolates the liquidity-leg definition while testing robustness of the leading result to a fuller, less selected sample. A near-equal result at higher coverage would be the more credible signal to carry forward.

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), 3)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(dlc, act), 3)))))

considered.reasoning: The leader smoothed the numerator only, leaving the denominator and the entire maturity leg at a single-year snapshot even though debt maturities cluster and a single year's dlc misstates a firm's structural rollover reliance. Smoothing both ratios tests whether the gain came from income noise specifically or from state persistence generally. The answer determines how the final generation should treat every flow leg.

considered.name: Smoothed Deep Fragility Maximum
considered.expression: MAX(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), MAX(RANK(RATIO(dlc, act)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine fragility requires persistently inadequate adjusted earnings, not one weak year; smoothing the coverage leg should stop the short leg from capturing innovators with temporary losses and concentrate it on chronically uncovered, goodwill-heavy borrowers.

Applying the smoothing that lifted the long side should raise the alpha magnitude and its reliability without sacrificing the slope. It repairs the one clear composition flaw remaining in the fragility aggregator.

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Only a sustained, repeatedly reported research program constitutes real knowledge capital; sporadic or absent R&D disclosure means there is no hidden asset to justify discounting the firm's accounting distress.

Used as a binding constraint rather than a tilt, persistence gates the long leg to genuine innovators while the other two legs verify that their solvency is real, which is the theme's exact conditional statement. It introduces the only untouched intangible measurement dimension available.

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), lt)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))))

Restored leverage measured against assets underperformed (fmb 3.11), but that version omitted accumulated equity entirely, so this is the untested middle case rather than a repeat. If it matches or beats 5.00, the final generation should build on an equity-cushion stock leg.

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Refinancing exposure is what binds for intangible-intensive firms, but it is properly measured as maturing debt relative to the whole asset base rather than relative to current assets, which are structurally tiny for research-intensive firms.

Rescaling by total assets keeps the maturity economics, restores coverage toward 0.142, and should make the long leg less selected — the one remaining structural flaw in the leading signal. This is the highest-value coverage repair available in the final round.

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))))

considered.reasoning: The persistence gate produced the archive's best alpha with full coverage but was tested without the restored-retained-earnings leg that drives every strong slope, so combining them targets both forms of evidence at once. Persistence is a qualifier on the *existence* of hidden knowledge capital rather than a tilt on its size, which is why it did not damage the slope the way intensity did. Depth stays at three, respecting the established optimum.

considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 5), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Because research payoffs arrive over multi-year horizons, the persistent component of an innovator's debt-service capacity is better measured over five years than three; longer averaging should further separate chronic weakness from investment-phase losses.

If five years continues the improvement, the mechanism is genuinely about the permanent component of earnings; if it reverses, three years is the correct horizon and staleness begins to dominate. Either outcome pins down the timing of the final specification.

Economically, consumer-facing brand builders are a second population of firms whose reported earnings and book equity understate economic capital, and they are currently misranked by every signal in the archive. considered.expression: MAX(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), MAX(RANK(RATIO(dlc, act)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(MA(ib, 3), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))))

Substituting total intangible share for goodwill share inside the MAX — rather than averaging it in as a tilt, which cost the slope — should raise the alpha without repeating that tradeoff.
